title: Editorial companion to the frozen staircase paper
author: Myeongjin Kang
scope: Nonblocking clarifications only; no paper edit or new theorem. Include with final package.

notes.clarification: The source presents a proof of its complex Saxl theorem; this project stipulates that upstream result. The following paper sentence already makes the project assumption explicit.

The pinned complex surjection dom:permutation-quotient, semisimplicity and Harman–Ryba Theorem 2.4 already yield complex regular containment. I21 supplies the stronger intermediate isomorphism. Neither route is new here.

The regular summand supplies at least dim(D) copies of each projective cover over a splitting field, not exact multiplicities in the full cube. The paper defines its coefficient-ring Specht module by scalar extension.

The non-projectivity comparison uses the classical hook-length dimension formula and divisibility of projective module dimensions by the Sylow order. The finite C7 control verifies divisibility patterns only; passing that divisibility test alone does not prove projectivity.
Equation (3.4) is the identity subsequently proved via Proposition 3; its product-of-coordinates expression follows immediately from the definition, while its delta value uses Proposition 3.

The symbols are local: D for a simple module in section 1, an ordered block in section 2, and calligraphic D for the retained alphabet in section 3; e_a denotes a word or a local basis letter as its index indicates.
z_(m,A) denotes the scalar-extended tensor 1 tensor z_m under the canonical tensor-cube identification.
The Ikenmeyer section and equation locators refer to arXiv:1410.6549v2, as specified in the bibliography and source map.

The PDF displays the not-equal symbol correctly, but text extraction can produce 6=. Readers should consult the included TeX for exact mathematical symbols. Accessibility improvement is deferred to a separately reviewed edition; frozen PDF bytes remain unchanged.
Equivariance of polytabloids gives g e_t = e_(gt); this is the identity underlying the common orbit-span description in section 2.
